# pr-1142 rework — CI `crap` quality gate fixed (9 owned CRAP violations)

## Issues/Notes

- The failed check on head `7b246940` is the **`crap` job** (`.github/workflows/quality.yml`): the per-function CRAP ratchet (crap4js, threshold 8) compares the head against the rolling `crap-baseline` release asset — "CRAP may only decrease".
- The log fetch failed on the CI side (`host callback returned invalid JSON`), so the job was **reproduced locally with the exact pinned toolchain** (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee620`, `nyc@17`, the released `crap-baseline.json` @ `main@f3782b2b`, same instrument → suite → ratchet procedure). The local ratchet block matched CI's verdict line-for-line (exit code 2, `CRAP may only decrease.`):
  - `REGRESSION js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::matchesGuards: 18.1 -> 19.1`
  - `REGRESSION js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 28 -> 30`
  - `NEW > 8` in `js/common/guestTransplant.js`: `guestPrTitle: 9`, `guestPrBody: 8.5`, `parseTransplantMarker: 12`, `parseLabelEvents: 14`, `validateGateWiring: 10`, `transplantSequence: 27`, `gcSteps: 10`
- The 27-CC `transplantSequence` was red even at 100 % statement coverage (CRAP = CC when fully covered), so the fix is behavior-preserving decomposition, not test-only work. Two helpers introduced by the first decomposition pass (`_labeledEventFor` CC 9, the shortened `transplantSequence` CC 10) were still over threshold and were split/trimmed further — every function now measures ≤ 8 at 100 % coverage.
- No open review threads exist (GraphQL census `graphqlTotal: 0`; the only listed thread is the informational bot red-head marker, excluded by policy), so no `review_replies` entries are due.
- Coverage-gap tests added first (TDD): the carried-labels branch of `guestPrBody`, the stateless-marker skip in `parseTransplantMarker`, the seen-set cycle guard in `transitivelyNeeds`, the empty-allowlist path of `classifyArmActor`, the >60-char/empty-login fallbacks of `sanitizeCoAuthor`, and a direct `matchesGuards` guard table (`prState` / `prMergeState` / merge-state lists / `crossRepo` true-path in-chain) — the suite grew 52 → 59 transplant tests (+166 smGithubSource file total).

## Approach

Every fix keeps the public module surface (`module.exports`) and all decision strings byte-identical; only internal composition changed.

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `matchesGuards` stays a flat guard table: the three merge-state guards collapsed behind one composite `_mergeStateGuardsFail`, `mergeable` + `prState` behind `_prStateGuardsFail` (CC 19 → 16, CRAP 19.1 → 16.0).
  - `queryPrs` (CC 30 → 26, CRAP 30.0 → 26.0): the gh-1140 `allowBlockedItems` branches moved into module-level `_blockedHoldVisible` / `_blockedQueryHoldFail`, and the inline `mutexMax` expression now reuses the pre-existing `_mutexMaxOf(q)` helper.
- `js/common/guestTransplant.js` — the decision core decomposed so each AC/edge case lives in one ≤ 8-CC helper:
  - `transplantSequence` (CC 27 → 8) → `_transplantSkipDecision` / `_transplantRefuseDecision` / `_parkResetDecision` / `_orphanDecision` / `_freshSequence`; the orchestrator resolves `cfg`/`source`/`base` once and walks the helpers in the original decision order.
  - `parseTransplantMarker` (12 → 8) → `_markerObject` (one comment body → marker-or-null).
  - `parseLabelEvents` (14 → 4) → `_parsedEventList` / `_labeledEventFor` / `_eventActorLogin`.
  - `validateGateWiring` (10 → 4) → `_jobsByIdOf` / `_wiringViolations`.
  - `gcSteps` (10 → 3) → `_gcEntryStep` / `_orphanStep`.
  - `guestPrTitle` (9 → 7): the duplicated `(cfg && cfg.titleMaxLen) || DEFAULTS.titleMaxLen` cap expression hoisted to one `cap` local (same value in both uses).
  - `guestPrBody` (8.5 → 8.0): behavior unchanged; the uncovered carried-verdicts branch is now covered by a test (CRAP = CC = 8 at 100 % coverage).

Final ratchet against the released baseline (local run, exact CI procedure):

```text
CRAP Ratchet
============
improved    js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::matchesGuards: 18.1 -> 16
improved    js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 28 -> 26
0 regression(s), 0 new over threshold, 2 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

## Files Modified

- `js/common/guestTransplant.js` — decision core and parse/gate/GC functions decomposed into ≤ 8-CC helpers (no export/behavior changes).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` — composite guard helpers + extracted blocked/mutexMax predicates in `matchesGuards`/`queryPrs`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_guestTransplant.js` — +7 tests for the previously uncovered branches (guestPrBody carried/degenerate payloads, stateless marker skip, sanitizeCoAuthor truncation/login fallback, transitivelyNeeds cycle, already-parsed event feed, empty machine-login allowlist).
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — +1 suite (+2 tests): direct provider-free `matchesGuards` guard table (prState/prMergeState/mergeState/notMergeState true-paths, crossRepo in-chain both ways).

## Owned CI violations — disposition

| CI ratchet item | Disposition |
|---|---|
| `githubSource.js::matchesGuards` 18.1 → 19.1 | fixed — composite guards, now 16.0 (improvement vs baseline) |
| `githubSource.js::queryPrs` 28 → 30 | fixed — extracted predicates + `_mutexMaxOf` reuse, now 26.0 (improvement vs baseline) |
| `guestTransplant.js::guestPrTitle: 9` | fixed — cap hoisted, now 7.0 @ 100 % |

| `guestTransplant.js::parseLabelEvents: 14` | fixed — 3-way split, now 4.0 @ 100 % |
| `guestTransplant.js::validateGateWiring: 10` | fixed — `_jobsByIdOf`/`_wiringViolations` split, now 4.0 @ 100 % |
| `guestTransplant.js::transplantSequence: 27` | fixed — 5-helper decomposition, now 8.0 @ 100 % |
| `guestTransplant.js::gcSteps: 10` | fixed — `_gcEntryStep`/`_orphanStep` split, now 3.0 @ 100 % |

## Test Coverage

- Reproduced CI job end-to-end locally: instrument (nyc@17) → full unit suite on the instrumented tree (`ci/run_with_coverage.js`) → `crap4js . --threshold 8 --baseline <released asset>` — **exit 0**, `0 regression(s), 0 new over threshold, 2 improvement(s)`.

- Canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` → **5603 passed, 0 failed** (exit 0); `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json` → **59 passed, 0 failed**.
- New tests run first (RED on the CRAP gate, tests pinning branch behavior), then the refactor kept them green; every refactored function reports **100 % statement coverage** in the Istanbul data.

Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Read input context:

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.

# pr-1142 rework — CI `crap` quality gate fixed (9 owned CRAP violations)

## Issues/Notes

- The failed check on head `7b246940` is the **`crap` job** (`.github/workflows/quality.yml`): the per-function CRAP ratchet (crap4js, threshold 8) compares the head against the rolling `crap-baseline` release asset — "CRAP may only decrease".
- The log fetch failed on the CI side (`host callback returned invalid JSON`), so the job was **reproduced locally with the exact pinned toolchain** (`IstiN/crap4js@83ee620`, `nyc@17`, the released `crap-baseline.json` @ `main@f3782b2b`, same instrument → suite → ratchet procedure). The local ratchet block matched CI's verdict line-for-line (exit code 2, `CRAP may only decrease.`):
  - `REGRESSION js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::matchesGuards: 18.1 -> 19.1`
  - `REGRESSION js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 28 -> 30`
  - `NEW > 8` in `js/common/guestTransplant.js`: `guestPrTitle: 9`, `guestPrBody: 8.5`, `parseTransplantMarker: 12`, `parseLabelEvents: 14`, `validateGateWiring: 10`, `transplantSequence: 27`, `gcSteps: 10`
- The 27-CC `transplantSequence` was red even at 100 % statement coverage (CRAP = CC when fully covered), so the fix is behavior-preserving decomposition, not test-only work. Two helpers introduced by the first decomposition pass (`_labeledEventFor` CC 9, the shortened `transplantSequence` CC 10) were still over threshold and were split/trimmed further — every function now measures ≤ 8 at 100 % coverage.
- No open review threads exist (GraphQL census `graphqlTotal: 0`; the only listed thread is the informational bot red-head marker, excluded by policy), so no `review_replies` entries are due.
- Coverage-gap tests added first (TDD): the carried-labels branch of `guestPrBody`, the stateless-marker skip in `parseTransplantMarker`, the seen-set cycle guard in `transitivelyNeeds`, the empty-allowlist path of `classifyArmActor`, the >60-char/empty-login fallbacks of `sanitizeCoAuthor`, and a direct `matchesGuards` guard table (`prState` / `prMergeState` / merge-state lists / `crossRepo` true-path in-chain) — the suite grew 52 → 59 transplant tests (+166 smGithubSource file total).

## Approach

Every fix keeps the public module surface (`module.exports`) and all decision strings byte-identical; only internal composition changed.

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `matchesGuards` stays a flat guard table: the three merge-state guards collapsed behind one composite `_mergeStateGuardsFail`, `mergeable` + `prState` behind `_prStateGuardsFail` (CC 19 → 16, CRAP 19.1 → 16.0).
  - `queryPrs` (CC 30 → 26, CRAP 30.0 → 26.0): the gh-1140 `allowBlockedItems` branches moved into module-level `_blockedHoldVisible` / `_blockedQueryHoldFail`, and the inline `mutexMax` expression now reuses the pre-existing `_mutexMaxOf(q)` helper.
- `js/common/guestTransplant.js` — the decision core decomposed so each AC/edge case lives in one ≤ 8-CC helper:
  - `transplantSequence` (CC 27 → 8) → `_transplantSkipDecision` / `_transplantRefuseDecision` / `_parkResetDecision` / `_orphanDecision` / `_freshSequence`; the orchestrator resolves `cfg`/`source`/`base` once and walks the helpers in the original decision order.
  - `parseTransplantMarker` (12 → 8) → `_markerObject` (one comment body → marker-or-null).
  - `parseLabelEvents` (14 → 4) → `_parsedEventList` / `_labeledEventFor` / `_eventActorLogin`.
  - `validateGateWiring` (10 → 4) → `_jobsByIdOf` / `_wiringViolations`.
  - `gcSteps` (10 → 3) → `_gcEntryStep` / `_orphanStep`.
  - `guestPrTitle` (9 → 7): the duplicated `(cfg && cfg.titleMaxLen) || DEFAULTS.titleMaxLen` cap expression hoisted to one `cap` local (same value in both uses).
  - `guestPrBody` (8.5 → 8.0): behavior unchanged; the uncovered carried-verdicts branch is now covered by a test (CRAP = CC = 8 at 100 % coverage).

Final ratchet against the released baseline (local run, exact CI procedure):

```text

============

improved    js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 28 -> 26
0 regression(s), 0 new over threshold, 2 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

## Files Modified

- `js/common/guestTransplant.js` — decision core and parse/gate/GC functions decomposed into ≤ 8-CC helpers (no export/behavior changes).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` — composite guard helpers + extracted blocked/mutexMax predicates in `matchesGuards`/`queryPrs`.
- `js/unit-tests/test_guestTransplant.js` — +7 tests for the previously uncovered branches (guestPrBody carried/degenerate payloads, stateless marker skip, sanitizeCoAuthor truncation/login fallback, transitivelyNeeds cycle, already-parsed event feed, empty machine-login allowlist).
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — +1 suite (+2 tests): direct provider-free `matchesGuards` guard table (prState/prMergeState/mergeState/notMergeState true-paths, crossRepo in-chain both ways).

## Owned CI violations — disposition

| CI ratchet item | Disposition |
|---|---|
| `githubSource.js::matchesGuards` 18.1 → 19.1 | fixed — composite guards, now 16.0 (improvement vs baseline) |
| `githubSource.js::queryPrs` 28 → 30 | fixed — extracted predicates + `_mutexMaxOf` reuse, now 26.0 (improvement vs baseline) |

| `guestTransplant.js::gcSteps: 10` | fixed — `_gcEntryStep`/`_orphanStep` split, now 3.0 @ 100 % |

## Test Coverage

- Reproduced CI job end-to-end locally: instrument (nyc@17) → full unit suite on the instrumented tree (`ci/run_with_coverage.js`) → `crap4js . --threshold 8 --baseline <released asset>` — **exit 0**, `0 regression(s), 0 new over threshold, 2 improvement(s)`.

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

### Path stability
Do not rename or move root `*.json` config files — CI workflows and Jira automations reference them by path. Safe refactors: splitting prompt markdown, adding instruction files, adding `cliPrompts` composition in target repos.

## Approach

Every fix keeps the public module surface (`module.exports`) and all decision strings byte-identical; only internal composition changed.

- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

  - `validateGateWiring` (10 → 4) → `_jobsByIdOf` / `_wiringViolations`.
  - `gcSteps` (10 → 3) → `_gcEntryStep` / `_orphanStep`.
  - `guestPrTitle` (9 → 7): the duplicated `(cfg && cfg.titleMaxLen) || DEFAULTS.titleMaxLen` cap expression hoisted to one `cap` local (same value in both uses).
  - `guestPrBody` (8.5 → 8.0): behavior unchanged; the uncovered carried-verdicts branch is now covered by a test (CRAP = CC = 8 at 100 % coverage).

## Files Modified

- `js/common/guestTransplant.js` — decision core and parse/gate/GC functions decomposed into ≤ 8-CC helpers (no export/behavior changes).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` — composite guard helpers + extracted blocked/mutexMax predicates in `matchesGuards`/`queryPrs`.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T15:23:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

The IT-transplant/IT-lanes/E2E-scratch legs (fake/live GitHub) stay environment-bound — their decision cores (plan, sequence, gate wiring, GC) are the UT-covered pure module; the transport is byte-pinned command builders.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. ## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6).
