decision=transplant reason=fresh
steps: create_ref → merge → open_pr → carry_decision → transplant_comment → close_pr
=> duplicate transplant: YES
```

The original sha re-merges and a **second `[guest #42] …` machine PR** opens, walking validate + review again — exactly the "second arm must be a no-op" case the snapshot semantics exist to prevent. With a hand-written `transplanted` marker the same replay yields `noop / already-transplanted`, so the core is right; the writer is missing. (This also undercuts round 1's "no `skipIfLabel` is correct — marker-based idempotency" rationale: that idempotency only covers the open/orphan states, not the completed one.)

**Suggested fix:** append a terminal marker step to the shared tail — e.g. `step('comment', { prNumber: source, text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'transplanted', source, head: sha, branch, transplant: <newPrNumber>, merged: <mergedSha> }) })` after `close_pr` in `transplantBodySteps`/`_resumeTailSteps` (the resume path needs it too — it currently leaves `armed` behind as well). {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1142
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1142
- **Title**: gh-1140 [GOAL] Guest fork PRs become machine PRs via po_accept transplant — zero fork CI, zero fork lanes (supersedes #1139)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1140` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T16:56:57Z

## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

The IT-transplant/IT-lanes/E2E-scratch legs (fake/live GitHub) stay environment-bound — their decision cores (plan, sequence, gate wiring, GC) are the UT-covered pure module; the transport is byte-pinned command builders.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD

**The gap.** The core's re-arm gate requires a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
// guestTransplant.js:736 (_parkResetDecision)
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) {
    return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', ... };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in this repo ever writes `state:"parked"` (grep over `js/`: only tests hand-craft it, e.g. `test_guestTransplant.js:443`). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker on the source is still the **`armed`** marker from the fresh sequence — so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code in production.** Next tick after a conflict park, with the guest's fixed head:

```
decision=skip reason=human-blocked
audit=guest-transplant: #42 skipped — blocked without a transplant park marker (human hold)
```

No rescue exists elsewhere: `blocked` is the fa#939 human-hold label and **no code path in this repo ever removes it** (grep `removeLabel.*blocked` → empty); the gh-994 head-change reset only clears `validation_failed` (`js/smAgent.js:2969`). The park comment's own promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head (parked-head reset)."* — is false. The `parked-head:` line is parsed by nothing on this lane.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments (unbounded spam).** The conflict fires at the `merge` step, *after* `create_ref` succeeded — so every conflict park strands an orphaned `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep then does: no PR on head → probe marker → newest = `armed` + head → `_orphanStep` returns `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry (round-1 fix) re-merges the **RECORDED stale sha** → 409 again → `parkSteps` again → **one duplicate `blocked` park comment per tick, forever**. And when the guest fixes their fork head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants:

re-entry decision=complete-orphan
re-entry merge step: headSha = aaaa… (the stale, conflicting sha)
```

1. In `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment: `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })` — `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone), and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed.
2. While there: `_parkResetDecision`'s steps merge `input.headSha` (the new head) but the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` (`js/smAgent.js:8566`) resolves the *marker's stale recorded sha* — once re-arm goes live, the close comment would name the wrong source sha. **dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no `state:"transplanted"` marker is ever written — reopening the closed source re-transplants it (duplicate machine PR)**

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```
parkSteps ops: add_label, comment
park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1140
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

The IT-transplant/IT-lanes/E2E-scratch legs (fake/live GitHub) stay environment-bound — their decision cores (plan, sequence, gate wiring, GC) are the UT-covered pure module; the transport is byte-pinned command builders.

  G --> V[validate-fresh then merge-validated - standard lanes]
  V --> GC[PR closed/merged - branch GC deletes ai/guest-N]
```

</details>

**The gap.** The core's re-arm gate requires a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
// guestTransplant.js:736 (_parkResetDecision)
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) {
    return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', ... };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in this repo ever writes `state:"parked"` (grep over `js/`: only tests hand-craft it, e.g. `test_guestTransplant.js:443`). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker on the source is still the **`armed`** marker from the fresh sequence — so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code in production.** Next tick after a conflict park, with the guest's fixed head:

```
decision=skip reason=human-blocked
audit=guest-transplant: #42 skipped — blocked without a transplant park marker (human hold)
```

No rescue exists elsewhere: `blocked` is the fa#939 human-hold label and **no code path in this repo ever removes it** (grep `removeLabel.*blocked` → empty); the gh-994 head-change reset only clears `validation_failed` (`js/smAgent.js:2969`). The park comment's own promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head (parked-head reset)."* — is false. The `parked-head:` line is parsed by nothing on this lane.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments (unbounded spam).** The conflict fires at the `merge` step, *after* `create_ref` succeeded — so every conflict park strands an orphaned `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep then does: no PR on head → probe marker → newest = `armed` + head → `_orphanStep` returns `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry (round-1 fix) re-merges the **RECORDED stale sha** → 409 again → `parkSteps` again → **one duplicate `blocked` park comment per tick, forever**. And when the guest fixes their fork head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants:

re-entry decision=complete-orphan
re-entry merge step: headSha = aaaa… (the stale, conflicting sha)
```

1. In `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment: `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })` — `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone), and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed.
2. While there: `_parkResetDecision`'s steps merge `input.headSha` (the new head) but the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` (`js/smAgent.js:8566`) resolves the *marker's stale recorded sha* — once re-arm goes live, the close comment would name the wrong source sha. Seed `usedSha` from the reset sha (or from the merge step's returned `mergedSha` context) instead.

Tests to add at the wiring level: replay `parkSteps` output + the armed marker through `parseTransplantMarker` → `transplantSequence` (head moved ⇒ `park-reset`; unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`), and a sweep-entry probe of a conflict-parked source ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`.

### Thread 12 — `js/common/guestTransplant.js` line 335

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no `state:"transplanted"` marker is ever written — reopening the closed source re-transplants it (duplicate machine PR)**

`_existingTransplantDecision` (`guestTransplant.js:699`) treats a `transplanted` marker as the terminal no-op — the snapshot-semantics anchor for AC5 ("a second `po_accept` on an already-transplanted source is a no-op with an audit line", ticket Invariants). 🚨 **BLOCKING: the GC sweep's `complete_orphan` (E5) can never complete — it always skips at the same-repo guard**

The sweep re-enters the full action with a **synthetic ticket whose `headRepo` is `null`**:

```js
transplantGuestPrAction(repoInfo, {
    prNumber: s.sourcePrNumber,
    title: '', author: '',
    labels: [cfg.label],
    headRepo: null, draft: false, state: 'OPEN'   // ← headRepo: null
}, cfg, []);
```

Inside `transplantSequence`, `_transplantRefuseDecision` runs the E3 cross-repo refusal **before** any orphan handling:

```js
if (!isCrossRepoHead(source.headRepo, base.owner, base.repo)) {
    return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'same-repo', ... };
}
```

`isCrossRepoHead(null, …)` returns `false` (fail closed), so the re-entry **always** produces `skip / same-repo`. Verified by replaying the exact sweep input through `transplantSequence`:

```
sweep complete_orphan re-entry decision: skip | reason: same-repo
main-path same state decision: complete-orphan | reason: orphan-branch-completed
```

Consequences:

- The sweep logs `🧩 completing orphan transplant on … (E5)` and then immediately logs `skipped — same-repo head` — contradictory audit output every tick.
- An armed-marker orphan whose source PR no longer matches the rule query (source closed by the guest, deleted, etc.) becomes a **permanent zombie**: the sweep keeps selecting `complete_orphan` for it (`_orphanStep` returns it for `state: 'armed'`), the action no-ops, and the branch is never completed **and never GC'd**.
- The main action path does complete orphans — but only while the source PR is still open, labeled, cross-repo and non-blocked, which is exactly the state the sweep's completion branch exists to cover when it no longer holds.

Suggested fix: make the sweep re-entry bypass the E3 refusal for marker-driven completion — either pass a synthetic cross-repo `headRepo` (`'__synthetic__/completion'`), or add an explicit `completionReentry: true` input that `_transplantRefuseDecision` honors (the arm actor was already vetted when the `armed` marker was written; note the re-entry already passes `machineLogins: []`, which today classifies any actor as human).

🚨 **BLOCKING: `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

This is the same wiring↔core mismatch class as round 1's finding: the decision core expects state the transport never produces. Verified by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`.

**The gap.** The core's re-arm gate requires a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
// guestTransplant.js:736 (_parkResetDecision)
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) {
    return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', ... };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in this repo ever writes `state:"parked"` (grep over `js/`: only tests hand-craft it, e.g. `test_guestTransplant.js:443`). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker on the source is still the **`armed`** marker from the fresh sequence — so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code in production.** Next tick after a conflict park, with the guest's fixed head:

```
decision=skip reason=human-blocked
audit=guest-transplant: #42 skipped — blocked without a transplant park marker (human hold)
```

No rescue exists elsewhere: `blocked` is the fa#939 human-hold label and **no code path in this repo ever removes it** (grep `removeLabel.*blocked` → empty); the gh-994 head-change reset only clears `validation_failed` (`js/smAgent.js:2969`). The park comment's own promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head (parked-head reset)."* — is false. The `parked-head:` line is parsed by nothing on this lane.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments (unbounded spam).** The conflict fires at the `merge` step, *after* `create_ref` succeeded — so every conflict park strands an orphaned `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep then does: no PR on head → probe marker → newest = `armed` + head → `_orphanStep` returns `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry (round-1 fix) re-merges the **RECORDED stale sha** → 409 again → `parkSteps` again → **one duplicate `blocked` park comment per tick, forever**. And when the guest fixes their fork head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants:

```
sweep step: [{"op":"complete_orphan","branch":"ai/guest-42","sourcePrNumber":42,"headSha":"aaaa…"}]
re-entry decision=complete-orphan
re-entry merge step: headSha = aaaa… (the stale, conflicting sha)
```

**Suggested fix (one change cures both):**
1. In `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment: `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })` — `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone), and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed.
2. While there: `_parkResetDecision`'s steps merge `input.headSha` (the new head) but the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` (`js/smAgent.js:8566`) resolves the *marker's stale recorded sha* — once re-arm goes live, the close comment would name the wrong source sha. Seed `usedSha` from the reset sha (or from the merge step's returned `mergedSha` context) instead.

Tests to add at the wiring level: replay `parkSteps` output + the armed marker through `parseTransplantMarker` → `transplantSequence` (head moved ⇒ `park-reset`; unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`), and a sweep-entry probe of a conflict-parked source ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```
parkSteps ops: add_label, comment
park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). On a real guest-transplant validation run, **nothing asserts the `needs:` gate wiring** — a project that enables `smGuestTransplant` but authors its workflow without the `needs:` prefix gets secret-consuming jobs on guest content with no gate, and no code anywhere notices.

The PR description's *"the ordering is enforced structurally in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) … impossible by construction"* overstates what the shipped code enforces: today it is a convention on the consuming project's workflow author, unenforced and undocumented as an integration contract.

2. **Document the contract**: name the project-side integration point (which hook calls `guestValidationDispatchPlan`, with which job-graph payload) in the rule description, so "asserted by UT on the dispatched job graph" refers to the real graph, not a synthetic fixture.

If confirmed as deliberate (gate purely project-side, checker is a library for `.dmtools/config.js` authors), a doc note in the rule description resolves this thread — as written, the description's wording overstates the enforcement.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```
parkSteps ops: add_label, comment
park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). The wiring (`transplantGuestPrAction`/`guestApplyStep`) calls only the plan/park/GC/parse helpers, and the validate-fresh dispatch itself neither reads the target workflow's job graph nor consults the checker before dispatching a guest-transplant leg. On a real guest-transplant validation run, **nothing asserts the `needs:` gate wiring** — a project that enables `smGuestTransplant` but authors its workflow without the `needs:` prefix gets secret-consuming jobs on guest content with no gate, and no code anywhere notices.

The PR description's *"the ordering is enforced structurally in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) … impossible by construction"* overstates what the shipped code enforces: today it is a convention on the consuming project's workflow author, unenforced and undocumented as an integration contract.

2. **Document the contract**: name the project-side integration point (which hook calls `guestValidationDispatchPlan`, with which job-graph payload) in the rule description, so "asserted by UT on the dispatched job graph" refers to the real graph, not a synthetic fixture.

If confirmed as deliberate (gate purely project-side, checker is a library for `.dmtools/config.js` authors), a doc note in the rule description resolves this thread — as written, the description's wording overstates the enforcement.

Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. The step order is `merge → open_pr → carry_decision → transplant_comment → close_pr`. If anything fails **between** `open_pr` and `close_pr` (a failed comment post, a failed close, a network blip), the state on the next tick is: source open with `po_accept`, armed marker, and an **open machine PR on the branch**.

That state is caught here, in `_transplantRefuseDecision`:

```js
if (input.openTransplantPr ||
    (input.marker && input.marker.state === 'transplanted')) {
    return { decision: 'noop', reason: 'already-transplanted', steps: [], ... };
}
```

- `openTransplantPr` truthy → permanent `noop`. The remaining steps (carry probe, transplant comment, source close) are **never re-run** — the AC1 close+comment lands only if a human closes the source by hand.
- The machine PR proceeds through validate/merge lanes **without the carried verdicts** (the carry labels, if due, were never applied), and the guest source PR stays open alongside it.
- Every subsequent tick re-queries the source and re-logs the same noop — silent, audit-only.

The decision core otherwise handles both neighbors of this gap well (pre-`open_pr` orphans complete via E5; post-close markers noop correctly). This is the only uncovered partial-failure window. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the E5 completion re-entry bypasses the fa#939 human-hold freeze**

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. Sequence: an arm happens (armed marker + branch cut), the tick dies pre-merge, and a human then adds `blocked` to the source (the fa#939 freeze — *"the machine skips the item ENTIRELY — all rules, all legs"*). The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the GC sweep's `complete_orphan` (E5) can never complete — it always skips at the same-repo guard**

The sweep re-enters the full action with a **synthetic ticket whose `headRepo` is `null`**:

```js
transplantGuestPrAction(repoInfo, {
    prNumber: s.sourcePrNumber,
    title: '', author: '',
    labels: [cfg.label],
    headRepo: null, draft: false, state: 'OPEN'   // ← headRepo: null
}, cfg, []);
```

Inside `transplantSequence`, `_transplantRefuseDecision` runs the E3 cross-repo refusal **before** any orphan handling:

```js
if (!isCrossRepoHead(source.headRepo, base.owner, base.repo)) {
    return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'same-repo', ... };
}
```

`isCrossRepoHead(null, …)` returns `false` (fail closed), so the re-entry **always** produces `skip / same-repo`. Verified by replaying the exact sweep input through `transplantSequence`:

```
sweep complete_orphan re-entry decision: skip | reason: same-repo
main-path same state decision: complete-orphan | reason: orphan-branch-completed
```

Consequences:

- The sweep logs `🧩 completing orphan transplant on … (E5)` and then immediately logs `skipped — same-repo head` — contradictory audit output every tick.
- An armed-marker orphan whose source PR no longer matches the rule query (source closed by the guest, deleted, etc.) becomes a **permanent zombie**: the sweep keeps selecting `complete_orphan` for it (`_orphanStep` returns it for `state: 'armed'`), the action no-ops, and the branch is never completed **and never GC'd**.
- The main action path does complete orphans — but only while the source PR is still open, labeled, cross-repo and non-blocked, which is exactly the state the sweep's completion branch exists to cover when it no longer holds.

Suggested fix: make the sweep re-entry bypass the E3 refusal for marker-driven completion — either pass a synthetic cross-repo `headRepo` (`'__synthetic__/completion'`), or add an explicit `completionReentry: true` input that `_transplantRefuseDecision` honors (the arm actor was already vetted when the `armed` marker was written; note the re-entry already passes `machineLogins: []`, which today classifies any actor as human).

🚨 **BLOCKING: `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

This is the same wiring↔core mismatch class as round 1's finding: the decision core expects state the transport never produces. Verified by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`.

**The gap.** The core's re-arm gate requires a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
// guestTransplant.js:736 (_parkResetDecision)
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) {
    return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', ... };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in this repo ever writes `state:"parked"` (grep over `js/`: only tests hand-craft it, e.g. `test_guestTransplant.js:443`). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker on the source is still the **`armed`** marker from the fresh sequence — so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code in production.** Next tick after a conflict park, with the guest's fixed head:

```
decision=skip reason=human-blocked
audit=guest-transplant: #42 skipped — blocked without a transplant park marker (human hold)
```

No rescue exists elsewhere: `blocked` is the fa#939 human-hold label and **no code path in this repo ever removes it** (grep `removeLabel.*blocked` → empty); the gh-994 head-change reset only clears `validation_failed` (`js/smAgent.js:2969`). The park comment's own promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head (parked-head reset)."* — is false. The `parked-head:` line is parsed by nothing on this lane.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments (unbounded spam).** The conflict fires at the `merge` step, *after* `create_ref` succeeded — so every conflict park strands an orphaned `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep then does: no PR on head → probe marker → newest = `armed` + head → `_orphanStep` returns `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry (round-1 fix) re-merges the **RECORDED stale sha** → 409 again → `parkSteps` again → **one duplicate `blocked` park comment per tick, forever**. And when the guest fixes their fork head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants:

```
sweep step: [{"op":"complete_orphan","branch":"ai/guest-42","sourcePrNumber":42,"headSha":"aaaa…"}]
re-entry decision=complete-orphan
re-entry merge step: headSha = aaaa… (the stale, conflicting sha)
```

**Suggested fix (one change cures both):**
1. In `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment: `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })` — `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone), and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed.
2. While there: `_parkResetDecision`'s steps merge `input.headSha` (the new head) but the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` (`js/smAgent.js:8566`) resolves the *marker's stale recorded sha* — once re-arm goes live, the close comment would name the wrong source sha. Seed `usedSha` from the reset sha (or from the merge step's returned `mergedSha` context) instead.

Tests to add at the wiring level: replay `parkSteps` output + the armed marker through `parseTransplantMarker` → `transplantSequence` (head moved ⇒ `park-reset`; unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`), and a sweep-entry probe of a conflict-parked source ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```
parkSteps ops: add_label, comment
park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). 🚨 **BLOCKING: the GC sweep's `complete_orphan` (E5) can never complete — it always skips at the same-repo guard**

The sweep re-enters the full action with a **synthetic ticket whose `headRepo` is `null`**:

```js

    prNumber: s.sourcePrNumber,
    title: '', author: '',

Inside `transplantSequence`, `_transplantRefuseDecision` runs the E3 cross-repo refusal **before** any orphan handling:

```js
if (!isCrossRepoHead(source.headRepo, base.owner, base.repo)) {
    return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'same-repo', ... };
}
```

`isCrossRepoHead(null, …)` returns `false` (fail closed), so the re-entry **always** produces `skip / same-repo`. Verified by replaying the exact sweep input through `transplantSequence`:

```
sweep complete_orphan re-entry decision: skip | reason: same-repo
main-path same state decision: complete-orphan | reason: orphan-branch-completed
```

Consequences:

Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). Fail closed exactly like `classifyArmActor` now does.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the E5 completion re-entry bypasses the fa#939 human-hold freeze**

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. Sequence: an arm happens (armed marker + branch cut), the tick dies pre-merge, and a human then adds `blocked` to the source (the fa#939 freeze — *"the machine skips the item ENTIRELY — all rules, all legs"*). The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```
parkSteps ops: add_label, comment
park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the E5 completion re-entry bypasses the fa#939 human-hold freeze**

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. Sequence: an arm happens (armed marker + branch cut), the tick dies pre-merge, and a human then adds `blocked` to the source (the fa#939 freeze — *"the machine skips the item ENTIRELY — all rules, all legs"*). The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```
parkSteps ops: add_label, comment
park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```

```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`).
