Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```
parkSteps ops: add_label, comment
park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). `guestValidationDispatchPlan` (this line) and `validateGateWiring` are exported and unit-tested (UT-gate) but **never invoked by any shipped code path**: grep over `js/` outside `unit-tests/` finds no caller of either. The wiring (`transplantGuestPrAction`/`guestApplyStep`) calls only the plan/park/GC/parse helpers, and the validate-fresh dispatch itself neither reads the target workflow's job graph nor consults the checker before dispatching a guest-transplant leg. On a real guest-transplant validation run, **nothing asserts the `needs:` gate wiring** — a project that enables `smGuestTransplant` but authors its workflow without the `needs:` prefix gets secret-consuming jobs on guest content with no gate, and no code anywhere notices.

The PR description's *"the ordering is enforced structurally in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) … impossible by construction"* overstates what the shipped code enforces: today it is a convention on the consuming project's workflow author, unenforced and undocumented as an integration contract.

Please either:
1. **Wire it**: at guest-transplant dispatch time, fetch the target workflow's job graph and refuse/fail the leg when `validateGateWiring(jobs, cfg.gate).ok === false`; or
2. **Document the contract**: name the project-side integration point (which hook calls `guestValidationDispatchPlan`, with which job-graph payload) in the rule description, so "asserted by UT on the dispatched job graph" refers to the real graph, not a synthetic fixture.

If confirmed as deliberate (gate purely project-side, checker is a library for `.dmtools/config.js` authors), a doc note in the rule description resolves this thread — as written, the description's wording overstates the enforcement.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the E5 completion re-entry bypasses the fa#939 human-hold freeze**

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. Sequence: an arm happens (armed marker + branch cut), the tick dies pre-merge, and a human then adds `blocked` to the source (the fa#939 freeze — *"the machine skips the item ENTIRELY — all rules, all legs"*). The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```
parkSteps ops: add_label, comment
park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). Fail closed exactly like `classifyArmActor` now does.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): the AC3 Security-Gate checker has zero callers — the "impossible by construction" gate boundary fires only in unit tests**

`guestValidationDispatchPlan` (this line) and `validateGateWiring` are exported and unit-tested (UT-gate) but **never invoked by any shipped code path**: grep over `js/` outside `unit-tests/` finds no caller of either. The wiring (`transplantGuestPrAction`/`guestApplyStep`) calls only the plan/park/GC/parse helpers, and the validate-fresh dispatch itself neither reads the target workflow's job graph nor consults the checker before dispatching a guest-transplant leg. On a real guest-transplant validation run, **nothing asserts the `needs:` gate wiring** — a project that enables `smGuestTransplant` but authors its workflow without the `needs:` prefix gets secret-consuming jobs on guest content with no gate, and no code anywhere notices.

The PR description's *"the ordering is enforced structurally in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) … impossible by construction"* overstates what the shipped code enforces: today it is a convention on the consuming project's workflow author, unenforced and undocumented as an integration contract.

Please either:
1. **Wire it**: at guest-transplant dispatch time, fetch the target workflow's job graph and refuse/fail the leg when `validateGateWiring(jobs, cfg.gate).ok === false`; or
2. **Document the contract**: name the project-side integration point (which hook calls `guestValidationDispatchPlan`, with which job-graph payload) in the rule description, so "asserted by UT on the dispatched job graph" refers to the real graph, not a synthetic fixture.

If confirmed as deliberate (gate purely project-side, checker is a library for `.dmtools/config.js` authors), a doc note in the rule description resolves this thread — as written, the description's wording overstates the enforcement.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the E5 completion re-entry bypasses the fa#939 human-hold freeze**

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. Sequence: an arm happens (armed marker + branch cut), the tick dies pre-merge, and a human then adds `blocked` to the source (the fa#939 freeze — *"the machine skips the item ENTIRELY — all rules, all legs"*). The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. **Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```
parkSteps ops: add_label, comment
park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the E5 completion re-entry bypasses the fa#939 human-hold freeze**

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. Sequence: an arm happens (armed marker + branch cut), the tick dies pre-merge, and a human then adds `blocked` to the source (the fa#939 freeze — *"the machine skips the item ENTIRELY — all rules, all legs"*). The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```

park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```

```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). ```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the E5 completion re-entry bypasses the fa#939 human-hold freeze**

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. Sequence: an arm happens (armed marker + branch cut), the tick dies pre-merge, and a human then adds `blocked` to the source (the fa#939 freeze — *"the machine skips the item ENTIRELY — all rules, all legs"*). The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

**Fixed — `parkSteps` now writes the `state:"parked"` machine marker beside the human comment** (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, round 3).

The writer was exactly the missing half you diagnosed: the park now posts three steps — `add_label` → human `parkComment` → a `comment` step carrying `transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason, actor })`. The parked marker is the newest snapshot, so:

- `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on a moved head (`park-reset`) and stays parked otherwise — AC4's auto re-arm is live, not dead code;
- `_orphanStep` routes a parked-marker orphan to `delete_ref` — the stranded conflict branch is GC'd instead of being re-completed every tick, so the per-tick duplicate park comment is gone;
- the wiring (`transplantGuestPrAction`) now pins `ctx.usedSha` from `sequenceHeadSha(seq)` — the merge step's OWN sha — so a park-reset close comment names the NEW head instead of the stale recorded sha (your second sub-point).

Pinned by wiring-level replays of your exact scenario in `test_guestTransplant.js` (round 3 suite): `parkSteps` output → `parseTransplantMarker` → `transplantSequence` — head moved ⇒ `park-reset`; unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked-marker branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`; and `sequenceHeadSha(park-reset seq) === new head`.

**Fixed — a terminal `state:"transplanted"` marker ends both shared tails** (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, round 3).

- `transplantBodySteps` (fresh path + E5 orphan completion) now ends `... close_pr → transplanted_marker`;
- `_resumeTailSteps` (the resume-after-open-pr path) ends the same way, pinning the recorded arm sha as the head.

The terminal op is rendered by the wiring (`guestApplyStep` case `transplanted_marker`) from the runtime ctx — the created PR number and merge sha exist only after the steps above ran — so the posted marker carries `transplant: <newPrNumber>`, `merged: <mergedSha>`, `head: <usedSha>`.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-20):

**Fixed — transplant markers are now machineAuthor-authenticated at parse time** (`parseTransplantMarker`, `js/common/guestTransplant.js`, round 3), following the repo's own gh-828 doctrine you cited.

One deliberate deviation from the suggested mechanism, in the trust-proof direction: the `actor` payload field alone could not secure this — the marker lives on the **guest's own PR**, so a forged `actor="<machine login>"` is as writable as the rest of the payload. The doctrine's real teeth are the comment **author**, which the guest cannot forge:

- `parseTransplantMarker(coments, trustedLogins)` now requires the machineAuthor allowlist; no allowlist / empty allowlist / a comment with no readable author → **no marker** (fail closed — a feed with only guest-authored markers reads as "no marker", so the fresh path re-arms from the human label event instead);
- author matching uses the exact `reviewVerdicts` spelling (`user.login || author.login || author.name`, lowercased, `[bot]` stripped) — same trust anchor as `readVerdictRecords`;
- the wiring (`guestMarker`) passes `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` on every probe — the action, the sweep's orphan probe, and the `completionRentry` re-entry all flow through it (the sweep now threads `machineLogins` through `sweepClosedGuestBranches` instead of the old `[]`);
- writers additionally stamp `actor: <first machineAuthor login>` into every marker they post (arm, parked, re-arm, transplanted) for audit and human rendering.

Pinned in the round 3 suite: forged-newest-vs-real-older feed → the recorded arm sha wins (E1 intact); empty/no allowlist → null; author-less comment → null; case/`[bot]` normalization; `resolveTransplantSha` on the authenticated feed still recorded-wins.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```
parkSteps ops: add_label, comment
park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). The PR description's *"the ordering is enforced structurally in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) … impossible by construction"* overstates what the shipped code enforces: today it is a convention on the consuming project's workflow author, unenforced and undocumented as an integration contract.

2. **Document the contract**: name the project-side integration point (which hook calls `guestValidationDispatchPlan`, with which job-graph payload) in the rule description, so "asserted by UT on the dispatched job graph" refers to the real graph, not a synthetic fixture.

If confirmed as deliberate (gate purely project-side, checker is a library for `.dmtools/config.js` authors), a doc note in the rule description resolves this thread — as written, the description's wording overstates the enforcement.

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. `_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the E5 completion re-entry bypasses the fa#939 human-hold freeze**

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. Sequence: an arm happens (armed marker + branch cut), the tick dies pre-merge, and a human then adds `blocked` to the source (the fa#939 freeze — *"the machine skips the item ENTIRELY — all rules, all legs"*). The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the E5 completion re-entry bypasses the fa#939 human-hold freeze**

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. Sequence: an arm happens (armed marker + branch cut), the tick dies pre-merge, and a human then adds `blocked` to the source (the fa#939 freeze — *"the machine skips the item ENTIRELY — all rules, all legs"*). The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

```

park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}

   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the E5 completion re-entry bypasses the fa#939 human-hold freeze**

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. Sequence: an arm happens (armed marker + branch cut), the tick dies pre-merge, and a human then adds `blocked` to the source (the fa#939 freeze — *"the machine skips the item ENTIRELY — all rules, all legs"*). The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

The writer was exactly the missing half you diagnosed: the park now posts three steps — `add_label` → human `parkComment` → a `comment` step carrying `transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason, actor })`. The parked marker is the newest snapshot, so:

- `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on a moved head (`park-reset`) and stays parked otherwise — AC4's auto re-arm is live, not dead code;
- `_orphanStep` routes a parked-marker orphan to `delete_ref` — the stranded conflict branch is GC'd instead of being re-completed every tick, so the per-tick duplicate park comment is gone;
- the wiring (`transplantGuestPrAction`) now pins `ctx.usedSha` from `sequenceHeadSha(seq)` — the merge step's OWN sha — so a park-reset close comment names the NEW head instead of the stale recorded sha (your second sub-point).

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): `parkSteps` never writes a `state:"parked"` machine marker — AC4's auto re-arm is unreachable, and every conflict park re-posts a duplicate park comment every tick**

Re-verified on the current head by replaying the exact transport-written state through `transplantSequence`:

```
parkSteps ops: add_label, comment
park comment carries machine marker payload: false
newest machine marker after park: {"state":"armed", …}
A) moved-head next tick: skip / human-blocked   (AC4 re-arm expected: park-reset)
B) sweep step for conflict-parked branch: complete_orphan headSha=<stale recorded sha>
   re-entry decision: complete-orphan → merge stale sha → 409 → parkSteps again
```

**The gap.** `_parkResetDecision` gates the re-arm on a machine marker with `state:"parked"`:

```js
var isOurPark = marker && marker.state === 'parked';
if (!isOurPark) return { decision: 'skip', reason: 'human-blocked', … };
```

But `parkSteps` (this line) posts only the **plain-text** `parkComment` — no `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload. Nothing in `js/` writes `state:"parked"` (only tests hand-craft it). After a conflict park, the newest machine marker is still the **`armed`** one from the fresh sequence, so the machine's own park is permanently misclassified as a *human hold*.

**Symptom A — AC4 re-arm is dead code.** With the guest's fixed head the next tick yields `skip / human-blocked`; no code path ever removes `blocked` from a parked source (fa#939 hold), so the park comment's promise — *"Re-arm happens automatically when a human push changes the head"* — is false.

**Symptom B — per-tick duplicate park comments.** The conflict fires at `merge`, *after* `create_ref` — every conflict park strands an orphan `ai/guest-<N>` branch with no PR. Each tick the GC sweep probes it: newest marker `armed` → `complete_orphan` → the `completionRentry` re-entry re-merges the **stale recorded sha** → 409 → `parkSteps` again → one duplicate `blocked` park comment **per tick, forever**. And once the guest fixes their head, the re-entry still merges the stale recorded sha (E1 recorded-wins beats the park-reset intent), so the fix never transplants.

**Fix (one change cures both):** in `parkSteps`, write the machine marker alongside the human comment — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'parked', source, head: ctx.headSha, branch, reason }) })`. `_orphanStep` then routes parked-marker orphans to `delete_ref` (branch GC'd, spam gone) and `_parkResetDecision` re-arms on the head change as designed. While there: seed the wiring's `ctx.usedSha` for the park-reset path from the **reset** sha (`js/smAgent.js:8567` currently resolves the marker's stale recorded sha), and pin both behaviors with wiring-level replays (parkSteps output → parse → sequence: head moved ⇒ `park-reset`, unchanged ⇒ `parked-head-unchanged`; sweep probe of a parked branch ⇒ `delete_ref`, not `complete_orphan`).

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). `guestValidationDispatchPlan` (this line) and `validateGateWiring` are exported and unit-tested (UT-gate) but **never invoked by any shipped code path**: grep over `js/` outside `unit-tests/` finds no caller of either. On a real guest-transplant validation run, **nothing asserts the `needs:` gate wiring** — a project that enables `smGuestTransplant` but authors its workflow without the `needs:` prefix gets secret-consuming jobs on guest content with no gate, and no code anywhere notices.

The PR description's *"the ordering is enforced structurally in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) … impossible by construction"* overstates what the shipped code enforces: today it is a convention on the consuming project's workflow author, unenforced and undocumented as an integration contract.

2. **Document the contract**: name the project-side integration point (which hook calls `guestValidationDispatchPlan`, with which job-graph payload) in the rule description, so "asserted by UT on the dispatched job graph" refers to the real graph, not a synthetic fixture.

If confirmed as deliberate (gate purely project-side, checker is a library for `.dmtools/config.js` authors), a doc note in the rule description resolves this thread — as written, the description's wording overstates the enforcement.

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): no `state:"transplanted"` marker is ever written — reopening the closed source re-transplants it (duplicate machine PR)**

`_existingTransplantDecision` (added in the round-1 rework) treats a `transplanted` marker as the terminal no-op, but the transport still never writes one: `buildTransplantComment` (this line) posts **plain text only**, and neither `transplantBodySteps` nor the new `_resumeTailSteps` appends a terminal marker step. Grep over `js/`: `state:"transplanted"` exists only in `markerHumanLine` rendering and test fixtures — zero writers.

Proven by replaying the post-transplant state (source closed, machine PR merged, branch GC'd per AC7, newest machine marker still `armed`), then the guest reopens their fork PR (always available — the fork branch is untouched):

```
decision=transplant reason=fresh
steps: create_ref → merge → open_pr → carry_decision → transplant_comment → close_pr
=> duplicate transplant: YES
```

The recorded sha re-merges and a **second `[guest #N] …` machine PR** opens, walking validate + review again — the exact "second arm must be a no-op" case the snapshot semantics exist to prevent. Same residue after a resume that succeeds at `close_pr` (the marker stays `armed` there too).

**Fix:** append the terminal marker to the shared tails — `step('comment', { text: transplantMarkerComment({ state: 'transplanted', source, head: sha, branch, transplant: <prNumber>, merged: <mergedSha> }) })` after `close_pr` in `transplantBodySteps` **and** in `_resumeTailSteps` — and pin it with a wiring-level test that parses the action's own posted comments back through `parseTransplantMarker` and asserts the second tick is a no-op.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (security, re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): transplant markers are not authenticated — the guest can forge a newer `armed` marker and redirect the transplant to a diff the human never vouched for**

`_markerObject` (this line) accepts **any** comment carrying the `<!-- guest-transplant … -->` payload — newest wins, no author check — and the marker lives on the **source PR, which is the guest's own PR**. Between the human's `po_accept` label and the SM tick (or after the arm marker lands), the guest posts a forged marker with any `SHA_RE`-valid sha:

```
<!-- guest-transplant state="armed" source="42" head="<any 40-hex sha>" branch="ai/guest-42" -->
```

Next tick the core reads it as the newest snapshot: `resolveTransplantSha` prefers the **recorded** sha, so the machine transplants attacker-chosen content while the audit line even says "RECORDED at arm time". Command injection is *not* possible (every consumption site re-validates through `SHA_RE`), but E1's post-arm pin is defeatable by the guest: a plain pre-tick force-push already lets unreviewed content in via the fresh path, and the forgery additionally breaks the recorded-sha protection *after* the machine armed.

This contradicts the repo's own marker doctrine, stated in `js/smAgent.js` (`readVerdictRecords`, ~line 6301): *"the marker format is public (this repo), so only markers authored by a configured machine login are trusted; an empty list trusts nothing (the machineAuthor doctrine)."* The verdict/rework markers follow it; the transplant marker doesn't.

**Fix:** record the writer identity in the marker (`actor: <login>` at write time — the wiring knows the machine login) and have `parseTransplantMarker` reject markers whose actor is not in the configured machineAuthor allowlist (pass `verdictMachineLogins(effectiveConfig)` into the probe — it is already resolved in `transplantGuestPrAction`). Fail closed exactly like `classifyArmActor` now does.
