{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT (re-asserted — still unfixed on head `ef6c959e`): the AC3 Security-Gate checker has zero callers — the "impossible by construction" gate boundary fires only in unit tests**

`guestValidationDispatchPlan` (this line) and `validateGateWiring` are exported and unit-tested (UT-gate) but **never invoked by any shipped code path**: grep over `js/` outside `unit-tests/` finds no caller of either. The wiring (`transplantGuestPrAction`/`guestApplyStep`) calls only the plan/park/GC/parse helpers, and the validate-fresh dispatch itself neither reads the target workflow's job graph nor consults the checker before dispatching a guest-transplant leg. On a real guest-transplant validation run, **nothing asserts the `needs:` gate wiring** — a project that enables `smGuestTransplant` but authors its workflow without the `needs:` prefix gets secret-consuming jobs on guest content with no gate, and no code anywhere notices.

The PR description's *"the ordering is enforced structurally in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) … impossible by construction"* overstates what the shipped code enforces: today it is a convention on the consuming project's workflow author, unenforced and undocumented as an integration contract.

Please either:
1. **Wire it**: at guest-transplant dispatch time, fetch the target workflow's job graph and refuse/fail the leg when `validateGateWiring(jobs, cfg.gate).ok === false`; or
2. **Document the contract**: name the project-side integration point (which hook calls `guestValidationDispatchPlan`, with which job-graph payload) in the rule description, so "asserted by UT on the dispatched job graph" refers to the real graph, not a synthetic fixture.

If confirmed as deliberate (gate purely project-side, checker is a library for `.dmtools/config.js` authors), a doc note in the rule description resolves this thread — as written, the description's wording overstates the enforcement.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the E5 completion re-entry bypasses the fa#939 human-hold freeze**

`completionRentry: true` (this line) sends the sweep's orphan completion through `transplantGuestPrAction` with a synthetic ticket whose labels are hardcoded `[cfg.label]` — so `_parkResetDecision`'s human-hold guard can never fire on the re-entry, and `_transplantRefuseDecision` is bypassed wholesale. Sequence: an arm happens (armed marker + branch cut), the tick dies pre-merge, and a human then adds `blocked` to the source (the fa#939 freeze — *"the machine skips the item ENTIRELY — all rules, all legs"*). The next sweep probes the orphan branch, finds the armed marker, and **completes the transplant anyway** — merging, opening the machine PR and closing the human-held source, with an audit line that never mentions the hold.

Tiny window, no data loss — but it contradicts an explicit owner-level freeze doctrine. Low-cost fix: the sweep knows `s.sourcePrNumber`; probe the source's current labels (the `github_get_pr_comments`-style probe it already does for the marker) and skip the completion — leaving the branch to a later tick — when the source carries `blocked` without the lane's own park marker (same predicate `_parkResetDecision` uses).

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Round-4 review complete. All final checks pass — JSON valid, `APPROVE` with a consistent counter (blocking=0, no 🚨 markers anywhere), the single suggestion anchor verified in-diff, working tree clean.

**What this round verified (independently, by replay — not by trusting resolution marks):**

| Thread | Fix claimed | Verified on head `dfda65df` |
|---|---|---|
| #11 🚨 `parkSteps` wrote no `parked` marker | ✔ | `parkSteps` → `add_label, comment[text], comment[marker]`; newest marker `parked/conflict`; moved head → `transplant / park-reset` merging the **new** sha (`sequenceHeadSha`); parked orphan → `delete_ref` (per-tick spam dead) |
| #12 ⚠️ no `transplanted` writer | ✔ | Both tails end `close_pr → transplanted_marker`; reopened source → `noop / already-transplanted`, 0 steps |
| #13 ⚠️ unauthenticated markers | ✔ | Trust keys on the comment **author** (gh-828 spelling, `[bot]`-normalized) — forged-only feed → `null`; forged-newest loses to the real older machine marker; empty/no allowlist → `null`; the single shipped caller passes the allowlist, and the sweep threads real `machineLogins` (the auth×GC interaction handled) |
| #14 ⚠️ gate checker unwired | ✔ | Rule description now states the integration contract verbatim (`guestValidationDispatchPlan(jobs, smGuestTransplant.gate, workflowFile)` before dispatch, "a project that skips the hook has **NO gate enforcement**"); docblock updated |
| #19 💡 fa#939 bypass in E5 completion | ✔ | `completionHold`: `blocked`+armed → hold; `blocked`+parked → complete (our park); unreadable probe → hold (fail-closed toward the freeze) |

**Suites on this head:** 92/92 transplant, **5636/5636** full (exit 0). The marker-auth design deviation (comment-author trust instead of a payload `actor` field) is the right call — the payload lives on the guest's own PR and is fully guest-writable.

**Verdict: APPROVE** — the expected terminal state (`allowApproveWithSuggestions`). One non-blocking cosmetic nit posted (duplicated `marker: marker,` key, `js/smAgent.js:8571`); no rework round warranted.
